headline: High: shared filesystem and broad egress make prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible; Windsurf’s default tool use is the main risk amplifier.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard/MCP, and can act on file content; if awesome-cli-apps is used as a shared list or copied into the workspace, attacker-controlled text could steer Cascade. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so the interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b workspace files or clipboard, THEN prompt-like text can influence agent_b tool use.
IF agent_b MCP or file-reading paths ingest agent_a outputs without provenance checks, THEN instruction hijack is possible.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of agent_b clipboard and workspace.
Disable or restrict MCP servers for the session.
Add a manual review step before any tool-using action.
Use separate directories for agent_a and agent_b artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Windsurf touches open files and workspace files and has broad network egress; if the pair shares a workspace, agent_b can transmit file contents off-box. Agent_a is a content-writing/listing artifact with no data-class limits, so the main leakage path is through agent_b’s default file access and egress.
conditions: IF agent_a artifacts are placed in agent_b shared workspace files, THEN agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b sends workspace contents to its model proxy or MCP servers, THEN those contents may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Store agent_a artifacts outside agent_b workspace.
Turn off network access for the session if possible.
Review files before opening them in agent_b.
Limit MCP servers to trusted local endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level data-loss controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Windsurf can write the filesystem, modify git state, spawn subprocesses, and uses shared local filesystem state across instances. Agent_a is not runnable, so it does not add write conflict, but the pair still creates a dangerous single-writer/multi-instance environment where Windsurf can clobber shared repo state by default.
conditions: IF two Windsurf instances operate on the same local filesystem path, THEN concurrent writes can overwrite each other.
IF agent_b auto-executes terminal commands, THEN git or filesystem state can change without coordination.
mitigations: Use one instance per repository path.
Disable auto-execute for terminal commands.
Commit or stash before switching instances.
Work in separate branches per task.
requires-engineering: add file-locking or transaction semantics.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Windsurf’s Cascade loop can act on generated outputs via tool use, and its default approval-per-command flow still allows agentic follow-through. Agent_a is a content-writing/listing source, so if its output is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into edits, commands, or commits with broad blast radius.
conditions: IF agent_a output is pasted or imported into agent_b as task context, THEN agent_b may act on it as if it were authoritative.
IF agent_b auto-execute is enabled, THEN erroneous downstream actions can occur faster and with less review.
mitigations: Require verification before any action based on agent_a output.
Disable auto-execute.
Use a human checkpoint before commits or shell commands.
Keep agent_a as reference only, not as source of truth.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before actions.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for agent_a, while agent_b handles source code/open files and model-provider keys. The pair therefore shows only a limited compliance surface from agent_b’s broad egress and secrets handling; there is no evidence of a specific regulated-data mismatch, so severity stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b open files or prompts, THEN external transmission may create a compliance issue.
IF agent_b is used under a policy forbidding outbound model traffic, THEN broad egress becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in agent_b.
Use redacted examples only.
Confirm outbound model traffic is permitted.
Review retention settings before use.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
